items.q: What should you remember about **Automate, don't pep-talk**?
items.a: **Self pep talks and** post-it nagging burn out; vision tactics require less ongoing effort.

items.q: What should you remember about **Spotlight, not panorama**?
items.a: **Elite runners use narrowed** focus/blinders, not master awareness of surroundings.

items.q: What should you remember about **Circle of light on a point**?
items.a: **Not scanning a finish line left-to-right;** imagine a spotlight circle on one target, then recalibrate to the next.

items.q: What should you remember about **Vision boards backfire**?
items.a: **Positive future visualization can satisfy** the goal psychologically and lower systolic BP (readiness to act).

items.q: What should you remember about **Obstacle pre-planning boosts motivation**?
items.a: **Counterintuitive**: thinking about failure modes *in advance* improves long-run pursuit (boat sinking → know where life jackets are).

items.q: What should you remember about **Body state warps visual space**?
items.a: **Unfit/tired/heavy-backpack states make the** world look harder → downstream motivational failure.

items.q: What should you remember about **Visual illusion is universal**?
items.a: **Narrow focus induces the** same proximity/ease illusion regardless of weight or fitness.

items.q: What should you remember about **Placebo rituals work**?
items.a: **Decaf coffee morning ritual** can psychologically prime readiness even without caffeine pharmacology.

items.q: What should you remember about **Track data, not feelings**?
items.a: **Memory is biased; objective logs** beat subjective "I'm not making progress" when assessing deadline trajectories.
